clue.text: Remain concerned with a certain arrogance

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or regarding, as in a letter heading
side is an old British word for swagger or putting on airs, as in 'no side about him'

explanation.surface: Someone stays on, preoccupied with a particular haughtiness.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE in the sense of pretentious airs is chiefly British; 'a certain' just marks that it is a particular kind of arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell or stay put somewhere, a synonym of remaining.

clue.text: Repair torn dress with a pin when speed is called for

indicators.note: something torn needs mending, so the letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Fix a ripped frock with a safety pin when you are in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair torn' rearranges DRESS and A PIN; 'with' joins them and 'when ... is called for' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidness is quickness or swiftness of movement.

clue.text: A personal voucher

parts.note: reads like a coupon or token, but means a person who vouches for someone

explanation.surface: A coupon issued to an individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voucher' means one who vouches, not a ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is a guarantor who backs or answers for another.

clue.text: Ends, mere ends — it's absurd

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, telling us to jumble the letters

parts.note: it's read as it is, giving IT with is as the link

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry that endings, only endings, are ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' shuffles MERE ENDS and IT; 'Ends' is a verb, as in settles or decides.
explanation.definitionFit: Determines means settles or decides, bringing a question to a close.

clue.text: Taking blockheads in, he's killing!

parts.note: an ass is a fool or dolt; the plural supplies one of the pair
the plural gives a second fool, another ass
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fooling a pair of idiots, he is having a riotous time.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'blockheads' supplies two ASSes; 'Taking' is a link. 'killing' pretends to mean hilarious, as in 'you're killing me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, someone whose work is slaying a target.

clue.text: Slightly injured, so didn't compete

definitions.meaning: grazed by a claw or thorn
withdrawn from a race before the start

explanation.surface: A runner has a minor wound and pulls out of the event.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse or athlete withdrawn before a race is said to be scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch is a minor wound, and to scratch is to withdraw an entrant from a contest.

clue.text: Troops get a bit warm yet stay cool

indicators.note: get a bit tells us to take a piece of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Soldiers are getting hot but must keep their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stay cool' is surface; the troops are hidden across 'warm yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Heavy drinker goes round the room to find something like an onion.-

indicators.note: goes round says the drinker surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A drunk wanders round the room looking for a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 8 down, but each answer stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small bulb of the onion family.

clue.text: —but there's no holding the non-drinker that's smart

indicators.note: holding means the first piece grips the second inside it

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
TT means teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: Continuing the drinkers' tale: the smart teetotaller cannot be stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) is a standard crossword abbreviation; 'but there's' and 'that's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and fashionable in dress.

clue.text: Dig in the earth for 30

definitions.meaning: points to the answer at 30 across, an angler's maggot

explanation.surface: Excavating soil to dig thirty holes.
explanation.walkthrough: A gentle (30 across) is a maggot used as fishing bait, so it is a grub.
explanation.definitionFit: To grub is to scrabble in soil, and a grub is a larva such as an angler's bait maggot.

clue.text: He plans to play outside left

indicators.note: the word outside says one piece sits round another, so the synonym for play wraps the abbreviation

parts.note: to potter is to play or pass time idly

explanation.surface: A man intends to go out and play on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside left' looks like a football position, but 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter is a schemer, someone who devises secret plans.

clue.text: Upright, but aggressive

definitions.meaning: in heraldry an animal shown rearing on its hind legs is described this way
violent and unrestrained, as in unchecked aggression

explanation.surface: A person is principled yet combative.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic beasts rearing up erect are rampant, and rampant also means wild, fierce and unrestrained.

clue.text: Hand out five hundred — one's donation

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
one's is read as one is, I being the Roman one, giving I + S
a tribute is a gift or payment offered

explanation.surface: Someone giving away five hundred pounds as a charitable gift.
explanation.walkthrough: "one's" is read as I (Roman one) plus S, rather than as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to share or deal out among people.

clue.text: Everybody stands by the youth-leader as a friend

indicators.note: stands by puts one piece next to the other, here directly after it

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word before the hyphen

explanation.surface: The whole group supports the leader of the youth club as a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'youth-leader' looks like a youth club organiser but just asks for the first letter of 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or supporter on your side.

clue.text: Like peas in a pod nevertheless

explanation.surface: Things look identical even so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means identical, and is also an idiom for even so or despite that.

clue.text: Sound covering for crawlers?

parts.note: the clue reads as insulation for creeping creatures, but splits into a hairpiece for the organ of hearing, naming small insects

explanation.surface: Soundproofing for creeping insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the insect's name into its two parts: wigs (coverings) for ears (organs of sound). The question mark flags the whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: These pincered insects' name, split up, describes hairpieces for the organs of hearing.

clue.text: American backing composer — he's really supportive

indicators.note: backing means turning back, so the short word for American is read from the end

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was an English composer of church music

explanation.surface: A US patron of a composer is very supportive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it reverses US into SU; STAINER is the Victorian composer of The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sustainer is one who upholds or props something up, a supporter.

clue.text: The carrier belted by a gunman

definitions.text: The carrier belted by a gunman

parts.words: The carrier belted by a gunman
parts.note: suggests a porter being beaten up by an armed man, but means the leather case for a pistol worn on a belt

explanation.surface: A porter is beaten up by an armed robber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belted' suggests being hit, but here means strapped on with a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger's pistol case hangs from the belt, so it is the carrier he wears belted on.

clue.text: Needs rice for cooking in the home

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are prepared or mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Rice is needed to cook at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' shuffles NEEDS RICE; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling or house.

clue.text: Showing craft about Danes being treated for depression

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other, so the ship letters surround the rest

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft

indicators.note: something being treated is being processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is seen tending Danish patients suffering from low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' is a ship, not a skill; 'being treated' makes an anagram of Danes, and 'about' puts the ship round it. 'Showing' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadness is low spirits or melancholy, which is what depression describes.

clue.text: Cleaner work-alternative — and dull

parts.note: to do is to work or perform
or introduces an alternative
mat, or matt, means without shine

explanation.surface: Housework as an alternative career seems boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person but is the mat on which shoes are wiped; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is where feet are wiped clean before entering a house.

clue.text: Doesn't like the setting of French exams

parts.note: de is the French word for of
tests are examinations

explanation.surface: Someone hates setting the papers for French examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setting' is a link here, pointing to how the pieces are laid out: French 'of' then exams.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe or dislike intensely.

clue.text: Laid out money without hesitation for a glider

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the spending wraps the pause

parts.note: spent means paid out
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone paid immediately for a sailplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' reads as immediately, but 'without' means outside here; a snake glides along.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake moves by sliding smoothly over the ground, so it is a glider.

clue.text: Murmur softly, softly in a confined area

parts.note: to coo is to make a soft murmuring sound, like a dove
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Whispering gently in a cramped space.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) is the musical marking for softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is a small pen or cage for keeping poultry, a cramped enclosure.

clue.text: This fellow caught and mounted insects

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means going upwards, so the insects are read bottom to top

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: A man caught insects and pinned them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' suggests displaying specimens, but in a down answer it reverses LICE into ECIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil is a man's first name, so it can name a particular man.

clue.text: Bars checking stock

parts.note: sounds like pubs doing a stocktake, but describes metal rails set in a road that stop livestock crossing

explanation.surface: Pubs doing an inventory of their supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' means livestock, not inventory; 'checking' means stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A road grating of parallel bars that farm animals will not walk over, so it halts livestock.

clue.text: To carry or, put another way, child-bearing

parts.note: a tot is a small child
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Carrying a baby, whichever way you put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child-bearing' reads as having a baby, but splits into a child and a compass bearing; 'or, put another way,' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to haul or lug something about.

clue.text: Story-teller the Bar upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A narrator distresses the legal profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Bar' looks like the legal profession but means RAIL; 'Story-teller' is a fibber.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells stories in the sense of fibs is someone who lies.

clue.text: An example of Flora as a writer of poetry

definitions.meaning: a type of plant, here a pink-flowered wild plant
Thomas ... was an Elizabethan poet and composer

explanation.surface: A girl called Flora is held up as a model poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Flora is capitalised to look like a name, but means plant life.
explanation.definitionFit: The campion is a wildflower, and Thomas Campion was an English Renaissance poet.

clue.text: Can include a red convertible for exchange

indicators.note: include says the can takes in the other letters within it

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A red convertible car might be part of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like the car but is the anagram signal for A RED, and 'include' puts the result inside the can.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is goods handed over as part payment for something new, a swap.

clue.text: Came down before time with lines learned

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: lit is the past tense of light, to land, as a bird lights on a branch
an era is a period of time
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Someone descended early, having memorised their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learned' (two syllables) is the definition, meaning bookish; RY for railway is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary means scholarly or concerned with books and writing.

clue.text: 9 is not unkind!

definitions.meaning: points to the answer at 9 down, a larva or maggot

explanation.surface: Claims that the number nine is kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A gentle is an angler's word for a maggot used as bait, which links it to the grub at 9.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle is a fly larva used as fishing bait, and gentle also means kind and mild.
